chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Kamil, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you begin the night prayer and have finished the opening, recite the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi) and the two Surahs of protection (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn), then recite the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha) and a Surah."

key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two Surahs of protection (Al-Falaq and An-Nas)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended order of Quranic recitation in the night prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific liturgical sequence for Salat al-Layl, emphasizing the recitation of Ayat al-Kursi and the Mu'awwidhat immediately after the opening supplication (Istiftah) to invoke divine protection before the main pillars of prayer. This order highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating supplication with Quranic recitation, ensuring spiritual preparedness through the 'two protections' before engaging with the Opening of the Book and the subsequent chapter.
